items.title: Expose managed asset root diagnostics in lattice check results
items.context: runManagedAssetCheck currently returns profile/assetMode/items/manifestPath only. Add stable JSON fields that identify the metadata/asset root, resolved gitRoot when available, and whether managed asset paths are relative to metadata root. Do not move asset writes to gitRoot; this is diagnostic clarity and evidence shape only.
items.userSees: lattice check --json includes explicit metadataRoot/assetRoot/gitRoot path-base diagnostics.

happy.desc: Run lattice check --json in a normal project and parse the root JSON object; assert explicit root diagnostics are present as stable machine-readable fields for metadataRoot, assetRoot, gitRoot, and the asset-path relativity flag/context rather than only being inferable from manifestPath or item relPath strings.

Verify the JSON root diagnostics identify metadataRoot/assetRoot as the base for managed asset relPath/applied paths while preserving the existing profile, assetMode, manifestPath, summary, and items fields for backward-compatible consumers.

edge.desc: Run lattice check --json where metadataRoot and configured gitRoot differ; assert metadataRoot and assetRoot resolve to the wrapper metadata root while gitRoot resolves to the configured repo root, with all fields explicit even when paths differ.

Run lattice check --json where gitRoot is absent or unavailable; assert the gitRoot diagnostic is still explicit as null/empty by contract and metadataRoot/assetRoot remain populated so callers never have to guess the path base.

adversarial.desc: Fail the item if the implementation only adds prose or nested per-item hints but no explicit root-level JSON diagnostics, because JSON consumers must not scrape text or reverse-engineer roots from relative paths.

Fail the item if adding gitRoot diagnostics changes relPath/applied path semantics or makes managed asset paths appear gitRoot-relative; diagnostics may explain gitRoot but must not redefine the asset root.

verificationEvidence.note: Build passed after commit b602ae20b; ManagedAssetCheckResult now includes metadataRoot, assetRoot, gitRoot, pathsRelativeTo, and assetRootGitRootSplit.
Focused wrapper-root smoke asserts check --json distinguishes metadataRoot, assetRoot, configured gitRoot, pathsRelativeTo=assetRoot, and split=true.

Focused smoke now runs an unconfigured, non-git metadataRoot before setting gitRoot and asserts check --json reports gitRoot as null while metadataRoot/assetRoot remain populated and pathsRelativeTo=assetRoot.
Focused smoke parses check --json and verifies metadataRoot/assetRoot are the managed asset path base while existing profile, assetMode, manifestPath, summary, and item relPath fields remain stable.
Smoke asserts root-level JSON diagnostics directly, including metadataRoot, assetRoot, gitRoot, pathsRelativeTo, and split flag, so consumers do not need to scrape prose or infer roots from relPath.

Split-root smoke verifies managed asset relPath/apply semantics remain assetRoot-relative: .lattice/Lattice.md is missing/applied under metadataRoot while configured gitRoot remains diagnostic context only.

items.title: Render clear path-base guidance in lattice check text output
items.context: renderManagedAssetCheck should show where relPath/applied/manifest paths are rooted, especially when metadataRoot != gitRoot. The text should make ClawCreek-style wrapper roots obvious before recommending check --apply.
items.userSees: lattice check text output explains that managed asset relPath values are relative to the metadata/asset root, and displays gitRoot when different.

happy.desc: Run lattice check in text mode and assert the output names the managed asset metadata/asset root and states that relPath, applied paths, and manifest paths are metadata-root or asset-root relative.
Verify the path-base guidance appears near the check summary for both clean and drift states so a human reading the default terminal output sees the root context before acting.

edge.desc: Run text output in a wrapper-root fixture where metadataRoot != gitRoot; assert the output shows both metadataRoot/assetRoot and gitRoot as separate paths and makes the difference visually clear.
Run text output when gitRoot equals metadataRoot or is unavailable; assert the guidance remains explicit without redundant or misleading split-root wording.

adversarial.desc: Fail the item if the text says or implies relPath values are gitRoot-relative, repo-root-relative, or cwd-relative when managed asset apply semantics remain metadata-root based.
Fail the item if check --apply is recommended before the output explains the path base, because wrapper-root users must know which root will be modified before applying managed assets.

verificationEvidence.note: Build passed after commit b602ae20b; renderManagedAssetCheck includes root guidance immediately after Summary for all check states.
Focused smoke asserts DRIFT and OK text place root guidance immediately after Summary, before apply recommendations or manifest output, and show configured gitRoot separately when split.
Smoke checks text guidance appears immediately after Summary for both DRIFT and OK states, before manifest/apply details, so humans see path-base context before acting.

verificationEvidence.command: node packages/main/dist/cli.js check 2>&1 | rg -n "Paths: managed asset relPath/applied/manifestPath values are relative to assetRoot\.|gitRoot: .*\(same as assetRoot\)"
verificationEvidence.note: Current worktree text output explicitly prints assetRoot-relative path guidance and marks gitRoot as same as assetRoot, covering the non-split case without misleading split-root wording.
Text assertions require the wording relative to assetRoot and, in split-root mode, say managed assets are not rooted at gitRoot, preventing repo/cwd/gitRoot-relative implication.
Smoke asserts root guidance is rendered before the apply recommendation, so wrapper-root users see which root will be modified before running check --apply.

items.title: Add wrapper-root regression coverage for lattice check diagnostics
items.context: Add a focused smoke/test that builds a non-git metadata root with configured gitRoot subdir and verifies check JSON/text identify assetRoot/metadataRoot separately from gitRoot while keeping relPath semantics unchanged.
items.userSees: A regression command proves wrapper-root lattice check diagnostics are explicit and apply semantics remain metadata-root based.

happy.desc: Add and run a focused regression command that creates a temporary wrapper-root fixture with non-git metadataRoot and configured gitRoot subdirectory; assert lattice check --json reports metadataRoot/assetRoot separately from gitRoot.
In the same regression, assert text output displays the split-root diagnostics and explains managed asset paths are metadata/asset-root relative.

edge.desc: Exercise the fixture with drift present and with managed assets already clean; assert diagnostics remain present in both states and item relPath values remain unchanged relative paths.

Run the regression on a metadataRoot path that is not itself a git repository; assert gitRoot discovery/configuration still appears only as diagnostic context and does not become the asset write root.

adversarial.desc: Run the regression with check --apply or the apply path helper and assert files are written/updated under metadataRoot/assetRoot, not under configured gitRoot, while gitRoot remains visible in diagnostics.

Fail the regression if it uses metadataRoot == gitRoot, checks only implementation internals, or validates only prose without parsing JSON root fields, because that would not protect the ClawCreek-style wrapper-root bug.

verificationEvidence.note: Focused smoke creates a temporary non-git metadataRoot with configured gitRoot subdir and verifies JSON/text diagnostics distinguish roots.
Focused smoke runs check --apply and asserts .lattice/Lattice.md plus .lattice/managed-assets.json are written under metadataRoot/assetRoot while gitRoot sentinel content remains unchanged.
Build passed with managed-assets-wrapper-root-smoke.ts compiled and exposed by package scripts.
Regression validates text output in the wrapper-root fixture, including split-root diagnostics and assetRoot-relative path-base guidance.
Regression fixture uses a metadataRoot that is not itself a git repository and a configured gitRoot subdirectory; assertions keep gitRoot diagnostic-only and asset writes under metadataRoot.
